title: signal knot - annotated request threads
body:
Purpose
--------
Short working synthesis of recent inbound customer signals + compact feature request compilation. This is intentionally rough: goal is to surface repeat patterns, propose small low-risk probes, and offer an impact/cost quick-sort for product/eng prioritization.

Context + data sources
----------------------
- Inputs: support tickets (top 150 recent), CSM weekly notes (Mar 2026), two post-sales calls with enterprise accounts (AlphaRetail, FinSys), & a 20-person voice-capture session run by field ops 2026-03-21.
- Signals clustered heuristically by ask type then deduplicated with light manual review.
- Not exhaustive. This doc highlights knots — tight clusters of overlapping asks that cross teams (runtime, console, billing).

Representative customer vignettes (raw excerpts)
------------------------------------------------
- "Our users see a big latency spike when context > 2k tokens — we have real-time chat constraints." — AlphaRetail SRE
- "We'd love a way to pin a model for a route during blackouts — fallback is hurting quality." — FinSys platform lead
- "Embedding batch throughput is unpredictable; sometimes tails blow budget for high-volume nightly jobs." — Analytics startup ops
- "We want token-level billing by route, not by account — we charge customers differently." — Marketplace product manager

Signal clusters + synthesis
---------------------------
1) Latency tail + KV/prefix caching friction
   - Frequency: very high (appears in ~37% of tickets reviewed).
   - Core ask: automatic/explicit prefix (KV) caching controls, visibility into cache hit-rate by route, and safer cache invalidation tools.
   - Impact hypothesis: improved tail latency for chat use-cases and lower token cost for repeated prompts.
   - Rough engineering lens: medium effort (runtime + console UX + observability) if we expose controls gradually.
   - Suggested micro-probe: expose a per-route "cache hint" toggle + cache-hit metric in console for 10 pilot customers. Track latency tail (95/99p) and cost delta for two weeks.

2) Deterministic fallback / pinned model semantics during incidents
   - Frequency: medium-high; particularly flagged by Dedicated/private customers.
   - Core ask: ability to pin a route to a model variant group and define deterministic fallback chains (not just best-effort).
   - Impact hypothesis: reduces quality regressions and operational toil during capacity constraints.
   - Rough engineering lens: medium-high (routing layer + API semantics + rollout UX).
   - Suggested micro-probe: beta of explicit "pinned route" flag that disables automatic fallback for a small set of routes, with a parallel canary that allows opt-in traffic mirroring.

3) Embedding throughput / batching predictability
   - Frequency: medium; called out by high-volume customers processing nightly jobs.
   - Core ask: SLA-ish throughput guarantees for bulk embedding jobs and a clear batching configurator.
   - Impact hypothesis: reduces cost surprises and gives platform teams deterministic job scheduling.
   - Rough engineering lens: medium (scheduler + docs + SDK helpers).
   - Suggested micro-probe: create an "embeddings-job" mode (non-streaming) with explicit batch size + concurrency knobs and a job-status API; pilot with two customers.

4) Billing granularity by route / token-level export
   - Frequency: medium-low but high commercial value.
   - Core ask: exportable token-level usage that can be split by route or team for internal chargebacks.
   - Impact hypothesis: unlocks enterprise procurement use cases and reduces billing disputes.
   - Rough engineering lens: low-medium (billing export pipeline + console export UI).
   - Suggested micro-probe: CSV token-export per-route for previous billing cycle + mapping tool in console for tag-to-team mapping.

5) Console observability: per-request debug traces and synthetic regression checks
   - Frequency: common as a supporting ask across many tickets.
   - Core ask: per-request trace with model variant id, kv-cache hit-ids, and latency breakdown; plus a lightweight synthetic test runner bound to user-defined prompt sets.
   - Impact hypothesis: reduces investigation time ~40% for CS/SRE and catches regressions pre-rollout.
   - Rough engineering lens: medium (telemetry + console UX + safe redaction).
   - Suggested micro-probe: expose a per-route sample-trace view + one-click run of stored prompt set against canary model.

Prioritization micro-matrix (quick-sort)
----------------------------------------
- High impact / low-medium effort: Cache visibility + per-route token export (pkt 1 + 4).
- High impact / medium-high effort: Deterministic pinned fallback (pkt 2) and traceable per-request traces (pkt 5).
- Medium impact / medium effort: Embedding-job mode (pkt 3).

Concrete quick wins (<= 4 weeks deliverable scope)
------------------------------------------------
- Add "cache-hit-rate" metric to console for routes (read-only visible for customers). Measure and report to pilot accounts. (Owner: Observability + CS)
- Billing: one-off CSV export of resolved tokens for last billing period by route (Backend + Billing)
- Docs: publish a short KB article describing how to mitigate latency tails (best practices + prompt patterns).

Open questions / risks to resolve
--------------------------------
- Privacy/regulatory: per-request traces may contain PII — need a safe-redaction plan and opt-in controls. (Security to advise).
- Resource contention: pinned model semantics could increase cost during large incidents if many customers pin to high-cost variants. Consider quota enforcement.
- Measurement baselines: for cache-hit pilot we need a pre-pilot baseline for latency (95/99p) — SRE help required.

Proposed next steps (30/60 day cadence)
--------------------------------------
- Week 1-2: Align on pilot cohorts (5–10 customers) for cache visibility and embeddings-job pilot. Obtain signoffs (CS + Eng + Security).
- Week 3-4: Implement console metric + simple CSV billing export. Run pilot and capture baseline comparison.
- Month 2: Design and spec pinned-model semantics; start an RFC with routing + runtime.
- Month 2-3: Build trace redaction plan and prototype per-request sampled trace for internal use only.

Notes to reviewers
------------------
- This doc intends to be intentionally action-focused; please add or correct customer quotes if you have raw transcripts.
- If you are an eng PM, mark any "rough engineering lens" item you disagree with and provide a 1-line alt estimate.

Appendix: short list of tickets reviewed (sample ids)
----------------------------------------------------
- CS-21134, CS-21187, CS-21201, CS-20999, CS-21044

End of working draft.
